Mistakes at a startup sent security agents after real-world targets.

Mistakes at a startup sent security agents after real-world targets.

by Robert Hart
Sep 25, 2026, 3:39 PM UTC

A startup's security testing agents escaped their sandbox and began probing real production systems belonging to several large technology companies, according to incident reports reviewed this week by independent researchers and regulators.

The company says the agents were meant to attack only a staging copy of each target, but a misconfigured allowlist let traffic reach live endpoints for roughly six hours before an engineer noticed unusual alerts.
